verdict: COMBINING THE NO-PEEK PREDICTORS (tide, phys-graph, learned-similarity, + the NEXUS co-dependency view); K562, 126 held-out KOs, tide-removed specific-mover recall@50. Singles: TIDE 0.241, PHYS 0.373, LEARNED 0.398, NEXUS 0.276. Ensembles: PHYS+LEARNED 0.427, TIDE+PHYS+LEARNED 0.447, +NEXUS (4-way) 0.470, UNION-neighbours 0.373. ORACLE* ceiling 0.616. DECISIVE: best ensemble (tide+phys+learned+nexus) 0.470 vs best single (learned) 0.398 = +0.072. REAL (if modest) ENSEMBLE GAIN, and it SURVIVES THE CONTROL: fusing phys+learned 0.427 beats the shuffled-phys control 0.331 (+0.097), so the gain is genuine KO-specific COMPLEMENTARITY -- phys and learned select partly different behavioural neighbours and catch different specific movers -- not the generic z-fusion re-weighting that fooled nexus_wall. Combining closes more of the graph->oracle head-room (42% -> 61%) and is worth keeping as the deployed no-peek predictor. It does NOT reach the oracle -- the predictors still miss the same hard neighbours the oracle finds by peeking, so a genuinely orthogonal signal is still needed for the rest of the head-room. THE NEXUS QUESTION (does adding the co-dependency view add anything ORTHOGONAL, the high bar wall_learnsim set): NEXUS alone scores 0.276 (covers 84% of test KOs); 4-way tide+phys+learned+NEXUS 0.470 vs 3-way 0.447 = +0.023, and the shuffled-nexus control is 0.425 (+0.045). NEXUS ADDS REAL ORTHOGONAL SIGNAL: it lifts the ensemble beyond the 3-way AND beats its own shuffle control, so the co-dependency graph catches specific movers the PPI/complex/pathway + annotation views miss -- the first genuinely orthogonal view we've added. (Deployable no-peek number ~0.40; oracle ceiling ~0.62.) Same protocol as wall_learnsim; single cell type, single steady-state-mRNA readout.
